overall_intent: A grounded fictional medical-horror photograph in which a reference-inspired woman encounters the hospital retaining control of her record at the ordinary point of discharge. Develop only useful local refinements at creativity 1; optional search material may be declined, and no new source is required to be adopted.

required_constraints: Retain a fictional clinical encounter charged with dread.
Retain the reference-inspired woman without asserting actual biography, diagnosis or inner life.
location.reason: A functional medical place must be readable so the fear comes from care and administration rather than a generic empty building.
location.expressive_goal: Make institutional access and patient-side waiting spatially evident through the hospital setting.
observable_targets: A discharge records counter dividing patient side and staff side
A clinical passage or exit connected to the waiting position
owner_relations: The woman occupies the public side of a hospital records interface.
The chart occupies the staff side beyond that interface.
preserved_choices: The frozen draft uses an after-hours discharge counter; this remains a preferred but replaceable authorial setting.
open_scope: Structural arrangement and medical-place cues within open setting and composition choices.
location.role_focus: A hospital discharge records interface that separates the waiting person from the retained chart, with an adjacent exit making controlled access legible.
location.scene_context: A reference-inspired woman has received an empty sleeve while her chart is visible beyond security glass. The scene is grounded, ordinary institutional space.

grounds.quote: An after-hours hospital discharge records counter and the adjacent closed exit.

review.author: Codex
review.rationale: This role develops physical place and structural access. It does not add a clinician, procedure, injury, or inferred world rule.

required_constraints: Retain a fictional clinical encounter charged with dread.

narrative_clue.reason: The failed return needs visible evidence that can be observed without claiming an unseen medical history.
narrative_clue.expressive_goal: Let an ordinary hospital record and its interrupted exchange imply loss of control at the shutter.
observable_targets: An empty record sleeve on the woman's side
A separate retained chart beyond a closed transfer interface
owner_relations: The sleeve is held by the woman on the public side.
The chart is a separate object on the staff side.
preserved_choices: The failed records exchange is the baseline direction; optional evidence may be refined without creating a new requester requirement.
open_scope: Visible owned clues and their placement or timing within the open authorial circumstances.
narrative_clue.role_focus: Visible evidence of a failed hospital records exchange: an empty returned sleeve and a retained chart on opposite sides of a closed handover boundary.
narrative_clue.scene_context: The patient-side woman has paused immediately after the sleeve was returned. The viewer should read withholding, while any exact chronology or institutional motive remains an interpretation.

grounds.quote: She receives an empty records sleeve and sees her chart retained behind security glass.

review.author: Codex
review.rationale: The clue role supports observed objects and relations. It does not turn a facial expression, stamp, or item into proof of a diagnosis, death, consent, or hidden prior event.

contact_point.reason: Hand contact is the physical hinge of the failed exchange and must remain coherent with the closed glass interface.
contact_point.expressive_goal: Keep the woman's interrupted reach bodily plausible and visibly on the patient side.
observable_targets: One hand holding the lightweight empty sleeve against the counter
Other fingertips resting on the patient-side lip of the closed hatch
owner_relations: Both hands belong to the same woman.
The sleeve and fingertips contact adjacent patient-side surfaces.
The separate chart remains beyond the glass rather than sharing a contact with her hands.
preserved_choices: The draft's two-hand counter arrangement is an optional way to show interruption; a compatible refinement may alter its exact geometry.
open_scope: Hand-object contact, reachable placement and boundary geometry in open action, pose and relationship choices.
contact_point.role_focus: A woman holds an empty sleeve at a hospital counter while her other fingertips linger on the closed transfer hatch; every hand, object and barrier remains separately owned and connected.
contact_point.scene_context: The person stands at a waist-height discharge records interface. The chart is visible on the staff side, beyond her reach.
